commit.message:
Reduce retry limit from 3 to 1: fail-open after first Codex failure

If Codex fails to produce a review, retrying won't help. Block once
to prompt Claude to run the script, then fail-open if still no review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add retry limit (3 attempts) before failing open on Codex failure

If Codex fails to produce a review file after 3 addressing-phase
attempts, the hook fails open instead of blocking indefinitely.
Retry count tracked via .claude/review-loop-retries file, cleaned
up on success, fail-open, and ERR trap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add timeout hint to retry message and prompt file guard to runner script

- Addressing-phase retry message now includes 600000ms timeout hint
  matching the task-phase message (prevents Codex being killed mid-review)
- Runner script checks prompt file exists before invoking Codex
  (fails fast with clear error instead of passing empty prompt)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Harden fail-open behavior in stop hook

- Transition failure now fails-open instead of continuing (prevents
  the phase staying as 'task' and re-running Codex on next stop)
- Addressing phase fails-open when both review file and runner script
  are missing (orphaned state from ERR trap cleanup)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address PR review feedback: verify review file before approving exit

- Addressing phase now checks review file exists before approving;
  blocks with instructions to run Codex script if missing (prevents
  skipping the review)
- ERR trap cleans up runner script and prompt file
- Remove dead re-entrancy guard (lock file is never written in new flow)
- Remove stale lock file references from AGENTS.md

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Update docs and cleanup for Codex runner script architecture

- README: reflect that hook prepares runner script, Claude runs Codex
  directly; update timeout from 900s to 30s
- review-loop.md: update instructions for new flow
- cancel-review.md: clean up runner script and prompt file on cancel
- stop-hook.sh: clean up runner script and prompt file in addressing
  and unknown-phase paths

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bump to v1.8.0: stream Codex output to user instead of hiding it

Move Codex execution from the stop hook into Claude's control. The hook
now writes a runner script and prompt file, then blocks Claude with
instructions to run it via Bash. This lets Codex output stream directly
to the user instead of being sent to /dev/null. Hook timeout reduced
from 900s to 30s since it no longer runs Codex itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bump version to 1.7.0: add lock file, atomic phase transitions, jq fallbacks

- Add PID-based lock file to prevent concurrent Codex launches
- Replace fragile sed phase transitions with atomic awk-based transition_phase()
- Add printf fallbacks on all jq calls to guarantee valid JSON output
- Clean up lock file on cancel, exit, and error paths

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Added an image to enhance the README content.

commit.message:
Add .gitattributes to enforce LF line endings on shell scripts

Fixes #2 — shell scripts with CRLF line endings cause "bash\r: No
such file or directory" on macOS/Linux. The current files are already
LF, but this prevents recurrence from Windows contributors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add update instructions to README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Move multi-agent setup to /review-loop command, validate in hook

Config changes now happen at invocation time (visible to user) instead
of silently in the stop hook. The /review-loop command:
- Checks codex is installed (errors if not)
- Auto-enables multi_agent in ~/.codex/config.toml (logs what it did)

The stop hook validates multi_agent is set and errors with manual
instructions if it was somehow disabled between setup and review.

README now includes manual config instructions.

Bumps to v1.6.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Auto-enable Codex multi-agent instead of erroring

Instead of blocking with setup instructions, the hook now
automatically enables multi_agent = true in ~/.codex/config.toml:
- No config file: creates one with [features] multi_agent = true
- Config exists but no multi_agent: appends to [features] section
- Already enabled: no-op

Bumps to v1.5.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Check for Codex multi-agent config before running review

The hook now validates that ~/.codex/config.toml exists and has
multi_agent = true. Three failure modes with clear fix instructions:
- No codex binary
- No config file
- Config exists but multi_agent not enabled

Error messages recommend the /experimental command as the easiest
path to enable multi-agent, with manual config as fallback.

Bumps to v1.4.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make Codex a hard dependency, remove self-review fallback

The whole point of the review loop is an independent second opinion.
Falling back to Claude self-review defeats that purpose. Now:
- Missing codex binary: blocks with install instructions
- Codex runs but no review file: blocks with retry guidance
- Both cases clean up state file so /review-loop can be re-run

Bumps to v1.3.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Document Codex multi-agent setup requirement in README

Users need `multi_agent = true` in ~/.codex/config.toml for parallel
review agents. Without it, Codex runs everything sequentially in a
single agent. Also updated review coverage section to show the 4-agent
architecture with conditional Next.js and UX agents.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Multi-agent code review with project-aware conditional agents

Split the single Codex review into parallel sub-agents:
- Agent 1 (Diff): focuses on git diff with detailed security, test, code quality criteria
- Agent 2 (Holistic): evaluates overall project structure, docs, agent harness
- Agent 3 (Next.js): conditional — App Router, caching, Server Actions, React perf
- Agent 4 (UX): conditional — agent-browser E2E testing for browser UI projects

Project type detection auto-enables Next.js and UX agents based on file presence.
Agents return findings as text; main agent deduplicates and writes consolidated review.

Bumps version to 1.2.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Remove version from marketplace.json, let plugin.json be source of truth
Bump version to 1.1.0

Inline setup logic in review-loop command

CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT env var is not available in bash commands from
command markdown files - it only gets substituted in hooks.json
command fields. Replace the external script call with an inline
bash setup command that doesn't need CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT resolution in review-loop command

- Quote the path: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/..."
- Use colon separator in allowed-tools: Bash(...:*) not Bash(... *)
- Match the pattern used by Ralph Wiggum plugin

Remove local dev install instructions from README

Update README with marketplace install instructions

Clarify agent-browser is only for projects with a web UI

Make the entire UX section skippable and scope agent-browser to

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address Codex self-review findings

- Add review_id regex validation to prevent path traversal (#3)
- Add telemetry logging to .claude/review-loop.log (#5, #6)
- Make codex flags configurable via REVIEW_LOOP_CODEX_FLAGS env var (#1)
- Add AGENTS.md with operating guidelines and CLAUDE.md symlink (#7)
- Add .gitignore for state/review artifacts (#8)
- OS-agnostic jq install instructions (#9)
- openssl fallback to /dev/urandom for ID generation (#10)
- Mark Codex as recommended, document fallback behavior (#11)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Initial implementation of review-loop plugin

Two-phase stop hook lifecycle:
1. Claude implements task, then stop hook runs Codex for independent review
2. Claude reads review, addresses feedback it agrees with, then exits

Features:
- Automatic Codex code review via stop hook
- Graceful fallback if Codex unavailable
- Duplicate loop prevention
- /cancel-review command
- 900s timeout for Codex review phase
